section.title: Required entries
section.para: The root directory of a DHS system MUST contain the following entries and SHOULD NOT contain others.

row.entry: The home directory of the root user.

section.title: Removable media
section.para: Removable media, such as USB drives and memory cards, are mounted in /run/media/user/label, where user is the user who mounted the medium and label is the label of its filesystem, or its UUID when it has no label. For example, a USB drive labelled ZAINIUM_DRIVE that the user alizain plugs in is found at /run/media/alizain/ZAINIUM_DRIVE.

The directory /run/media/user SHOULD be readable only by that user and by root. Removable media MUST NOT be mounted inside /overlayer: they belong to no layer, and a medium mounted there could hide or replace files of the system. /media is not used.
This is the place where udisks mounts media on most Linux systems, so desktop file managers and their users find them where they expect.

section.title: Entries that must not exist
section.para: The following FHS directories MUST NOT exist at the root, neither as directories nor as symbolic links: /usr, /bin, /sbin, /lib, /lib32, /lib64, /libx32, /etc, /var and /boot. Their contents live in the layers; lists where.
Keeping these names absent is what makes the layers enforceable: a program cannot write into /usr/lib and thereby into the base, because there is no such directory to write into.
